 [0m[1m[4m[38;2;240;198;116mThe History of Roads[0m                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                       
 Roads are humanity's oldest infrastructure, enabling trade, communication, and conquest. The earliest roads were      
 simple animal trails widened by repetitive use, later deliberately constructed by ancient civilizations.              
                                                                                                                       
 The Romans built the most sophisticated road system of the ancient world, with over 250,000 miles of roads connecting 
 their vast empire. Roman roads featured layered construction-stone foundations, gravel, and surfaces-remarkably       
 durable engineering that some remain usable today. These roads facilitated military movement, trade, and cultural     
 exchange.                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                       
 Medieval Europe saw road infrastructure decline. Most travel occurred on poorly maintained tracks until the 18th      
 century, when toll roads and turnpikes funded systematic improvements. The Industrial Revolution demanded better      
 transportation networks, spurring road construction innovations.                                                      
                                                                                                                       
 The 19th and 20th centuries transformed roads completely. Macadam surfaces, asphalt, and concrete replaced dirt and   
 stone. The automobile's rise necessitated modern highway systems. The Interstate Highway System, begun in 1956,       
 revolutionized American transportation and commerce.                                                                  
                                                                                                                       
 Today's roads integrate technology-smart highways with real-time traffic monitoring. From ancient footpaths to        
 digital-age expressways, roads remain civilization's backbone, connecting communities and enabling global commerce.
